title: Irregular yo forms: hacer, salir, poner, saber, ver
summary: Verbs that are regular except for an odd first person: hago, salgo, pongo, sé, veo.
focus: Present tense of hacer, salir, poner, traer, saber, conocer, ver, dar
content:
## Only the yo form is odd

Several very common verbs are regular in every person except **yo**.

| verb | yo | the rest (regular) |
|---|---|---|
| **hacer** (to do, make) | **hago** | haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen |
| **salir** (to go out, leave) | **salgo** | sales, sale, salimos, salís, salen |
| **poner** (to put) | **pongo** | pones, pone, ponemos, ponéis, ponen |
| **traer** (to bring) | **traigo** | traes, trae, traemos, traéis, traen |
| **saber** (to know facts) | **sé** | sabes, sabe, sabemos, sabéis, saben |
| **conocer** (to know people/places) | **conozco** | conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocéis, conocen |
| **ver** (to see) | **veo** | ves, ve, vemos, veis, ven |
| **dar** (to give) | **doy** | das, da, damos, dais, dan |

## Hacer: do, make, and more

- *¿Qué haces?* (What are you doing?)
- *Hago la cama.* (I make the bed.)
- *Hace calor.* (It's hot. This is weather.)
- *Hacer deporte, hacer los deberes, hacer una pregunta.*

## Saber or conocer?

- **saber**: facts, information, how to do something: *Sé la respuesta. Sé nadar.* (I can swim)
- **conocer**: being familiar with people and places: *Conozco a tu hermano. Conozco Madrid.*

Note the **personal a** before a person: *Veo **a** María. Conozco **a** tu hermano.*

## Salir and poner in daily life

- *Salgo de casa a las ocho.* (I leave home at eight.)
- *Salimos con amigos los viernes.* (We go out with friends on Fridays.)
- *Pongo la mesa.* (I set the table.) *Pongo la tele.* (I turn the TV on.)

quiz.explanation: The yo form has a g: hago.
Only yo is irregular; tú is regular: haces.
Saber's yo form is sé, with an accent.

quiz.prompt: ___ a tu hermano. (I know your brother.)
quiz.explanation: Knowing a person is conocer: conozco, with the personal a.

quiz.prompt: ___ nadar. (I can swim / I know how to swim.)
quiz.explanation: Knowing how to do something is saber: sé nadar.

quiz.prompt: ___ la tele por la noche. (I watch…)
Nosotros ___ de casa a las ocho.
quiz.explanation: Salir is a regular -ir verb outside yo: salimos.

listening.note: Saber + infinitive = to know how to.

listening.text: Veo la tele por la noche.
Hago los deberes por la tarde.
listening.meaning: I do my homework in the afternoon.

listening.text: Conozco bien la ciudad de Sevilla.
listening.meaning: I know the city of Seville well.
listening.note: Conocer for places and people, saber for facts.

listening.text: Traigo el pan y pongo la mesa.
listening.meaning: I bring the bread and set the table.

listening.text: Doy un paseo por el parque los domingos.
listening.meaning: I go for a walk in the park on Sundays.
listening.note: New word: el paseo = the walk, as in dar un paseo.

listening.text: Hago la cama todas las mañanas antes de salir.
listening.meaning: I make the bed every morning before going out.

listening.text: Los viernes salgo con mis amigos y no hago los deberes hasta el domingo.
listening.meaning: On Fridays I go out with my friends and don't do my homework until Sunday.

conversations.title: A normal evening
conversations.scenario: Teresa and Iván talk about what they do after work.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: What do you do after work?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Salgo del trabajo a las seis y hago deporte.
lines.meaning: I leave work at six and do sport.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Yo pongo la tele y veo las noticias.
lines.meaning: I turn on the TV and watch the news.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Do you know how to cook?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sé hacer tortilla, nada más. ¿Conoces el restaurante nuevo?
lines.meaning: I can make tortilla, that's all. Do you know the new restaurant?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No lo conozco. ¿Salimos a cenar el viernes?
lines.meaning: I don't know it. Shall we go out for dinner on Friday?

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Yes. I'll bring my sister, ok?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro. Le doy la dirección mañana.
lines.meaning: Sure. I'll give her the address tomorrow.

bites.title: The yo-go verbs
bites.rule: Hacer, salir, poner and traer are irregular only in yo, and they all add a g: hago, salgo, pongo, traigo. Every other person is regular.
bites.example: Salgo de casa y hago deporte.
bites.example_meaning: I leave home and do sport.

bites.title: Other odd yo forms
bites.rule: These yo forms follow no single pattern: saber becomes sé (with an accent), ver becomes veo, dar becomes doy and conocer becomes conozco.
bites.example: Sé nadar y veo la tele.
bites.example_meaning: I can swim and I watch TV.

bites.title: Saber vs conocer
bites.rule: Use saber for facts and skills (sé la respuesta, sé nadar). Use conocer for being familiar with people and places (conozco Madrid). A person takes the personal a.

bites.title: Hacer has many uses
bites.rule: Hacer means do and make, and it also describes the weather: hago la cama, hago los deberes, hace calor.

sorts.title: Saber or conocer?
sorts.why: Facts and skills take saber. People and places you are familiar with take conocer.

sorts.title: Real yo form or wrong form?
sorts.why: The yo forms are hago, salgo, pongo, sé, veo and conozco. The regular-looking versions do not exist.

sorts.title: Hago, pongo or salgo?
sorts.why: You make (hacer) the bed and do homework, set (poner) the table and turn the TV on, and go out (salir) of places or with people.

spots.sentence: Yo haco los deberes por la tarde.
spots.why: Hacer's yo form has a g: hago.

spots.sentence: Siempre salo de casa a las ocho.

spots.why: Saber's yo form is sé, with an accent.
Use conocer, not saber, to say you know a person.

spots.sentence: Por la noche vo la tele.
Yo pono la mesa a las nueve.

builds.text: Pongo la tele y veo las noticias.
builds.meaning: I turn on the TV and watch the news.

builds.text: Salgo del trabajo a las seis.

builds.meaning: I know how to make tortilla.
